blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

The docs-freshness check regenerates `docs/agents/generated/*` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails if the committed docs differ. The PR adds new JS files/tests but doesn't regenerate the docs. Let me check whether running the generator produces a diff on this branch.
{"command":"node js/agentDocGenerator.js && git status --porcelain docs/"}

/**
 * Shared git merge-state probes (gh-761).
 *
 * A conflicted merge of the base branch sits unconcluded in the working tree
 * (MERGE_HEAD present) until someone deliberately resolves or aborts it:
 * the rework setup leaves that state for the CLI agent on purpose, and the
 * agent's own `git merge origin/main` can be mid-conflict at any tick.
 *
 * Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before
 * touching the tree (same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js —
 * duplicated probes drift):
 *   - js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js — a blind `git add -A && git commit`
 *     would stage the unmerged paths (conflict markers included) and
 *     FINALIZE the foreign merge as a 'WIP auto-save' commit pushed to
 *     origin: silent branch corruption flowing into validation/review.
 *   - js/common/pullRequest.js syncBranchWithBase — `git merge` on top of
 *     MERGE_HEAD fails ("You have not concluded your merge") and the
 *     resolveMergeConflicts/abort fallback would then auto-resolve — or
 *     silently abort — the agent's in-flight merge.
 *   - js/storyTestAutomationRework.js mergeMain — same finalize-a-foreign-
 *     merge hazard through its --ours/--theirs auto-resolution.
 *
 * `runCommand` follows the (command, workingDir) convention shared with
 * common/pullRequest.js — pass the site's cli_execute_command wrapper so the
 * probe executes in the SAME working directory as the commit/merge it gates.
 *
 * GraalJS-compatible: var/plain functions only, no Node APIs.
 */

/**
 * True when MERGE_HEAD resolves — a merge is in progress in that working tree.
 *
 * Real git prints the merge-head SHA and exits 0 when MERGE_HEAD exists; it
 * exits 1 (cli_execute_command throws) when it doesn't. Requiring non-empty
 * output in addition to a non-throwing call keeps loose test doubles that
 * return '' for unknown commands on the "not in progress" path.
 */
function isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir) {
    if (typeof runCommand !== 'function') return false;
    try {
        var out = runCommand('git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD', workingDir);
        return !!(out && String(out).trim());
    } catch (e) {
        return false; // exit 1 — no MERGE_HEAD, the normal case
    }
}

module.exports = {
    isMergeInProgress: isMergeInProgress
};

Now I have a good picture. Several other merge/abort sites exist that consult no probe:

1. `js/common/gitOps.js detectMergeConflicts` — intentionally LEAVES a conflicted merge state for the agent (by design). This is the origin of the MERGE_HEAD state. Not a hazard per se.

2. `js/preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js:81` — `git merge origin/baseBranch --no-edit`, fallback `git merge --abort`. Same auto-abort/resolve hazard as syncBranchWithBase had. Not covered by the PR.

3. `js/pushReworkChanges.js:326` — `git merge --no-edit origin/<branchName>` on push failure; `syncWithBase` in preCli*Setup does rebase/merge with `--abort` fallbacks. Not covered.

4. `js/smAgent.js` silent refresh — `git merge` push (line 1276 area uses fetch + merge-base check; let me check where the actual merge happens).

5. `js/postTestReworkResults.js:225` — `git merge origin/<baseBranch> --no-commit --no-ff`.

The PR's doc comment in mergeState.js says "Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before touching the tree" — but only 3 of the ~6 sites do. The PR description says "every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it". That's an overclaim — `preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup`, `postTestReworkResults`, `pushReworkChanges` merge sites, and smAgent silent refresh don't consult the probe.

However, scope-wise: the ticket is about the autosave timer and merge-main steps. The severity of the missed sites:
- `preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js` — this runs at setup (before the agent), typically on a fresh checkout. But rework setups may run on an existing working dir where a conflicted merge was left. If MERGE_HEAD exists, `git merge origin/base --no-edit` fails with "you have not concluded your merge", then the catch does `git merge --abort` — aborting the agent's in-flight resolution. Same hazard class.
- `postTestReworkResults.js:225` — similar.

These are pre-existing gaps, not regressions of this PR. The PR narrows the race for the most dangerous site (blind autosave commit) and two merge sites. Missing sites = IMPORTANT (incomplete fix per its own "every commit- or merge-producing site" canon), not blocking. This is a key finding: `js/postTestReworkResults.js:87` already has a **pre-existing local `isMergeInProgress()`** with the exact same probe (`git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — but it returns **true when the command succeeds and false when it throws** — WITHOUT the non-empty-output requirement the new canonical helper has. The PR created a canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` claiming "one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites (duplicated probes drift)" but did NOT refactor `postTestReworkResults.js` to use it. This is exactly the duplication/drift the PR's own rationale warns against. That's an IMPORTANT finding (duplication, inconsistent semantics: the local one returns true on empty output + exit 0, though real git prints the SHA so it's mostly equivalent — but loose test doubles could differ).

Also there are other merge sites not covered:
1. `js/preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js:81` — merge with abort fallback, no probe.
2. `js/pushReworkChanges.js:326` — `git merge --no-edit origin/<branch>` on push retry, no probe (though syncBranchWithBase earlier in the same flow now has the probe — the flow: pushReworkChanges calls syncBranchWithBase FIRST, which now refuses when MERGE_HEAD exists, and only later does the `git merge origin/<branchName>` sync-push. So the earlier gate partially covers the flow. But `git merge --no-edit origin/<branchName>` merges the REMOTE branch of the SAME name into local — on top of an unconcluded merge this fails with "you have not concluded your merge" — and here the error just throws (no auto-abort), so it fails loudly. OK.
3. `js/postTestReworkResults.js:225` — has its own local isMergeInProgress guard already (pre-existing): `if (!mergeInProgress && prIsDirty)` — it skips starting a merge when one is in progress, then `stageUnmergedPaths` + commit "If a merge is in progress this creates the merge commit" — this one deliberately FINALIZES an in-progress merge. Hmm wait — that's the intended behavior there? "Commit. If a merge is in progress this creates the merge commit." So postTestReworkResults finalizes the agent's concluded-but-uncommitted merge. That's deliberate: the agent resolved conflicts, and post-test-rework commits them. OK.
4. `js/preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js:81` — has `git merge --abort` fallback — same auto-abort hazard that syncBranchWithBase just fixed. Missing coverage. IMPORTANT.
5. `js/smAgent.js` silent refresh merge — let me check.

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #761
### What changed
Mid-merge safety for the WIP autosave and the merge-main steps (gh-761): the 5-minute timer no longer commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, and every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it.

### Key decisions
- New canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` (`isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir)` via `git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites, same rationale as `gitStaging.js`
- Timer (`timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`): probe runs **before** the dirty-tree check (a mid-merge status is always dirty) and after the base-branch guard; the tick skips commit+push but still uploads the session artefact (git-independent crash-safety)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (publish-time merge): refuses as its **first** decision with `mergeInProgress: true` — previously a leftover `MERGE_HEAD` made the fallback auto-resolve or silently `git merge --abort` the agent's in-flight resolution
- `storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain`: refuses (throws actionable error) instead of `--ours`/`--theirs`-auto-committing a foreign merge with baked conflict markers

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 1659 passed, 0 failed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_timerAutoCommitAndSave.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_storyTestAutomationRework.json
node js/test/git_remote_tracking_ref.test.js
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[5-min timer tick] --> P{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P -->|yes| S[skip add/commit/push — artefact still uploaded]
  P -->|no| C[WIP auto-save commit + push]
  PUB[publish merge-main] --> P2{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P2 -->|yes| R[refuse: mergeInProgress error to ticket]
  P2 -->|no| M[git merge --no-edit origin/base]
  REW[test-rework mergeMain] --> P3{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P3 -->|yes| E[throw actionable refusal]
  P3 -->|no| M2[merge origin/main + auto-resolve]
```

</details>

## Description

This time the merge was clean (marker scan on the branch tip: no `<<<<<<<` in dart/yaml). Same pattern on fa #1231 (saves 09:58/10:03 → merge 219f96f).

**The risk:** the autosave ticks blindly. If a merge of main CONFLICTS mid-leg, the next tick's `git add -A && git commit` will either (a) error out mid-merge (harmless but noisy), or (b) finalize the merge and bake unresolved conflict markers into a 'WIP auto-save' commit — silent branch corruption that then flows into validation/review as if it were deliberate work.

**Fix:** the autosave must skip its tick when MERGE_HEAD exists (git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD), and the merge-main step must refuse to start on a dirty tree (or autosave-then-merge atomically). Owner raised it: 'автокомиты сломаются или нет в такой ситуации?'

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

blocks.text:
/**
 * Shared git merge-state probes (gh-761).
 *
 * A conflicted merge of the base branch sits unconcluded in the working tree
 * (MERGE_HEAD present) until someone deliberately resolves or aborts it:
 * the rework setup leaves that state for the CLI agent on purpose, and the
 * agent's own `git merge origin/main` can be mid-conflict at any tick.
 *
 * Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before
 * touching the tree (same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js —
 * duplicated probes drift):
 *   - js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js — a blind `git add -A && git commit`
 *     would stage the unmerged paths (conflict markers included) and
 *     FINALIZE the foreign merge as a 'WIP auto-save' commit pushed to
 *     origin: silent branch corruption flowing into validation/review.
 *   - js/common/pullRequest.js syncBranchWithBase — `git merge` on top of
 *     MERGE_HEAD fails ("You have not concluded your merge") and the
 *     resolveMergeConflicts/abort fallback would then auto-resolve — or
 *     silently abort — the agent's in-flight merge.
 *   - js/storyTestAutomationRework.js mergeMain — same finalize-a-foreign-
 *     merge hazard through its --ours/--theirs auto-resolution.
 *
 * `runCommand` follows the (command, workingDir) convention shared with
 * common/pullRequest.js — pass the site's cli_execute_command wrapper so the
 * probe executes in the SAME working directory as the commit/merge it gates.
 *
 * GraalJS-compatible: var/plain functions only, no Node APIs.
 */

/**
 * True when MERGE_HEAD resolves — a merge is in progress in that working tree.
 *
 * Real git prints the merge-head SHA and exits 0 when MERGE_HEAD exists; it
 * exits 1 (cli_execute_command throws) when it doesn't. Requiring non-empty
 * output in addition to a non-throwing call keeps loose test doubles that
 * return '' for unknown commands on the "not in progress" path.
 */
function isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir) {
    if (typeof runCommand !== 'function') return false;
    try {
        var out = runCommand('git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD', workingDir);
        return !!(out && String(out).trim());
    } catch (e) {
        return false; // exit 1 — no MERGE_HEAD, the normal case
    }
}

module.exports = {
    isMergeInProgress: isMergeInProgress
};

The PR claims "every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it". But it only touched 3 sites: timer, syncBranchWithBase (pullRequest.js), storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain. The ticket asks about the autosave and merge-main steps. Let me check these other sites to see whether they're candidates for the same hazard:

- `preCliMobileTestAutomationSetup.js:81` — merge in test automation setup for mobile. If MERGE_HEAD exists at setup start... this runs `git merge origin/baseBranch --no-edit`. If a merge is already in progress, the merge will fail with "You have not concluded your merge" and then `git merge --abort` will run — aborting the agent's (or setup's) in-flight merge. Mid-merge safety for the WIP autosave and the merge-main steps (gh-761): the 5-minute timer no longer commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, and every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it.

### Key decisions
- New canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` (`isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir)` via `git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites, same rationale as `gitStaging.js`
- Timer (`timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`): probe runs **before** the dirty-tree check (a mid-merge status is always dirty) and after the base-branch guard; the tick skips commit+push but still uploads the session artefact (git-independent crash-safety)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (publish-time merge): refuses as its **first** decision with `mergeInProgress: true` — previously a leftover `MERGE_HEAD` made the fallback auto-resolve or silently `git merge --abort` the agent's in-flight resolution
- `storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain`: refuses (throws actionable error) instead of `--ours`/`--theirs`-auto-committing a foreign merge with baked conflict markers

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 1659 passed, 0 failed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_timerAutoCommitAndSave.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_storyTestAutomationRework.json
node js/test/git_remote_tracking_ref.test.js
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[5-min timer tick] --> P{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P -->|yes| S[skip add/commit/push — artefact still uploaded]
  P -->|no| C[WIP auto-save commit + push]
  PUB[publish merge-main] --> P2{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P2 -->|yes| R[refuse: mergeInProgress error to ticket]
  P2 -->|no| M[git merge --no-edit origin/base]
  REW[test-rework mergeMain] --> P3{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P3 -->|yes| E[throw actionable refusal]
  P3 -->|no| M2[merge origin/main + auto-resolve]
```

</details>

# gh-761: WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)

## Description

**Live sequence (fa PR #1311, branch ai/gh-1308, 2026-10-06):** WIP auto-saves at 10:27/10:32/10:37 (5-min cadence), then 'Merge branch main' commit 9a7e2ae as tip. This time the merge was clean (marker scan on the branch tip: no `<<<<<<<` in dart/yaml). Same pattern on fa #1231 (saves 09:58/10:03 → merge 219f96f).

**The risk:** the autosave ticks blindly. If a merge of main CONFLICTS mid-leg, the next tick's `git add -A && git commit` will either (a) error out mid-merge (harmless but noisy), or (b) finalize the merge and bake unresolved conflict markers into a 'WIP auto-save' commit — silent branch corruption that then flows into validation/review as if it were deliberate work.

**Fix:** the autosave must skip its tick when MERGE_HEAD exists (git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD), and the merge-main step must refuse to start on a dirty tree (or autosave-then-merge atomically). Owner raised it: 'автокомиты сломаются или нет в такой ситуации?'

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

The docs-freshness check regenerates `docs/agents/generated/*` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails if the committed docs differ. The PR adds new JS files/tests but doesn't regenerate the docs. Let me check whether running the generator produces a diff on this branch.

/**
 * Shared git merge-state probes (gh-761).
 *
 * A conflicted merge of the base branch sits unconcluded in the working tree
 * (MERGE_HEAD present) until someone deliberately resolves or aborts it:
 * the rework setup leaves that state for the CLI agent on purpose, and the
 * agent's own `git merge origin/main` can be mid-conflict at any tick.
 *
 * Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before
 * touching the tree (same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js —
 * duplicated probes drift):
 *   - js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js — a blind `git add -A && git commit`
 *     would stage the unmerged paths (conflict markers included) and
 *     FINALIZE the foreign merge as a 'WIP auto-save' commit pushed to
 *     origin: silent branch corruption flowing into validation/review.
 *   - js/common/pullRequest.js syncBranchWithBase — `git merge` on top of
 *     MERGE_HEAD fails ("You have not concluded your merge") and the
 *     resolveMergeConflicts/abort fallback would then auto-resolve — or
 *     silently abort — the agent's in-flight merge.
 *   - js/storyTestAutomationRework.js mergeMain — same finalize-a-foreign-
 *     merge hazard through its --ours/--theirs auto-resolution.
 *
 * `runCommand` follows the (command, workingDir) convention shared with
 * common/pullRequest.js — pass the site's cli_execute_command wrapper so the
 * probe executes in the SAME working directory as the commit/merge it gates.
 *
 * GraalJS-compatible: var/plain functions only, no Node APIs.
 */

/**
 * True when MERGE_HEAD resolves — a merge is in progress in that working tree.
 *
 * Real git prints the merge-head SHA and exits 0 when MERGE_HEAD exists; it
 * exits 1 (cli_execute_command throws) when it doesn't. Requiring non-empty
 * output in addition to a non-throwing call keeps loose test doubles that
 * return '' for unknown commands on the "not in progress" path.
 */
function isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir) {
    if (typeof runCommand !== 'function') return false;
    try {
        var out = runCommand('git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD', workingDir);
        return !!(out && String(out).trim());
    } catch (e) {
        return false; // exit 1 — no MERGE_HEAD, the normal case
    }
}

module.exports = {
    isMergeInProgress: isMergeInProgress
};

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-761 WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-761` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #761
### What changed
Mid-merge safety for the WIP autosave and the merge-main steps (gh-761): the 5-minute timer no longer commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, and every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it.

### Key decisions
- New canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` (`isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir)` via `git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites, same rationale as `gitStaging.js`
- Timer (`timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`): probe runs **before** the dirty-tree check (a mid-merge status is always dirty) and after the base-branch guard; the tick skips commit+push but still uploads the session artefact (git-independent crash-safety)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (publish-time merge): refuses as its **first** decision with `mergeInProgress: true` — previously a leftover `MERGE_HEAD` made the fallback auto-resolve or silently `git merge --abort` the agent's in-flight resolution
- `storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain`: refuses (throws actionable error) instead of `--ours`/`--theirs`-auto-committing a foreign merge with baked conflict markers

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 1659 passed, 0 failed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_timerAutoCommitAndSave.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_storyTestAutomationRework.json
node js/test/git_remote_tracking_ref.test.js
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[5-min timer tick] --> P{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P -->|yes| S[skip add/commit/push — artefact still uploaded]
  P -->|no| C[WIP auto-save commit + push]
  PUB[publish merge-main] --> P2{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P2 -->|yes| R[refuse: mergeInProgress error to ticket]
  P2 -->|no| M[git merge --no-edit origin/base]
  REW[test-rework mergeMain] --> P3{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P3 -->|yes| E[throw actionable refusal]
  P3 -->|no| M2[merge origin/main + auto-resolve]
```

</details>

# gh-761: WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)

## Description

**Live sequence (fa PR #1311, branch ai/gh-1308, 2026-10-06):** WIP auto-saves at 10:27/10:32/10:37 (5-min cadence), then 'Merge branch main' commit 9a7e2ae as tip. This time the merge was clean (marker scan on the branch tip: no `<<<<<<<` in dart/yaml). Same pattern on fa #1231 (saves 09:58/10:03 → merge 219f96f).

**The risk:** the autosave ticks blindly. If a merge of main CONFLICTS mid-leg, the next tick's `git add -A && git commit` will either (a) error out mid-merge (harmless but noisy), or (b) finalize the merge and bake unresolved conflict markers into a 'WIP auto-save' commit — silent branch corruption that then flows into validation/review as if it were deliberate work.

**Fix:** the autosave must skip its tick when MERGE_HEAD exists (git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD), and the merge-main step must refuse to start on a dirty tree (or autosave-then-merge atomically). Owner raised it: 'автокомиты сломаются или нет в такой ситуации?'

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

The docs-freshness check regenerates `docs/agents/generated/*` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails if the committed docs differ. The PR adds new JS files/tests but doesn't regenerate the docs. Let me check whether running the generator produces a diff on this branch.

/**
 * Shared git merge-state probes (gh-761).
 *
 * A conflicted merge of the base branch sits unconcluded in the working tree
 * (MERGE_HEAD present) until someone deliberately resolves or aborts it:
 * the rework setup leaves that state for the CLI agent on purpose, and the
 * agent's own `git merge origin/main` can be mid-conflict at any tick.
 *
 * Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before
 * touching the tree (same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js —
 * duplicated probes drift):
 *   - js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js — a blind `git add -A && git commit`
 *     would stage the unmerged paths (conflict markers included) and
 *     FINALIZE the foreign merge as a 'WIP auto-save' commit pushed to
 *     origin: silent branch corruption flowing into validation/review.
 *   - js/common/pullRequest.js syncBranchWithBase — `git merge` on top of
 *     MERGE_HEAD fails ("You have not concluded your merge") and the
 *     resolveMergeConflicts/abort fallback would then auto-resolve — or
 *     silently abort — the agent's in-flight merge.
 *   - js/storyTestAutomationRework.js mergeMain — same finalize-a-foreign-
 *     merge hazard through its --ours/--theirs auto-resolution.
 *
 * `runCommand` follows the (command, workingDir) convention shared with
 * common/pullRequest.js — pass the site's cli_execute_command wrapper so the
 * probe executes in the SAME working directory as the commit/merge it gates.
 *
 * GraalJS-compatible: var/plain functions only, no Node APIs.
 */

/**
 * True when MERGE_HEAD resolves — a merge is in progress in that working tree.
 *
 * Real git prints the merge-head SHA and exits 0 when MERGE_HEAD exists; it
 * exits 1 (cli_execute_command throws) when it doesn't. Requiring non-empty
 * output in addition to a non-throwing call keeps loose test doubles that
 * return '' for unknown commands on the "not in progress" path.
 */
function isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir) {
    if (typeof runCommand !== 'function') return false;
    try {
        var out = runCommand('git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD', workingDir);
        return !!(out && String(out).trim());
    } catch (e) {
        return false; // exit 1 — no MERGE_HEAD, the normal case
    }
}

module.exports = {
    isMergeInProgress: isMergeInProgress
};

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-761 WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-761` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #761
### What changed
Mid-merge safety for the WIP autosave and the merge-main steps (gh-761): the 5-minute timer no longer commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, and every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it.

### Key decisions
- New canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` (`isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir)` via `git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites, same rationale as `gitStaging.js`
- Timer (`timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`): probe runs **before** the dirty-tree check (a mid-merge status is always dirty) and after the base-branch guard; the tick skips commit+push but still uploads the session artefact (git-independent crash-safety)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (publish-time merge): refuses as its **first** decision with `mergeInProgress: true` — previously a leftover `MERGE_HEAD` made the fallback auto-resolve or silently `git merge --abort` the agent's in-flight resolution
- `storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain`: refuses (throws actionable error) instead of `--ours`/`--theirs`-auto-committing a foreign merge with baked conflict markers

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 1659 passed, 0 failed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_timerAutoCommitAndSave.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_storyTestAutomationRework.json
node js/test/git_remote_tracking_ref.test.js
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[5-min timer tick] --> P{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P -->|yes| S[skip add/commit/push — artefact still uploaded]
  P -->|no| C[WIP auto-save commit + push]
  PUB[publish merge-main] --> P2{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P2 -->|yes| R[refuse: mergeInProgress error to ticket]
  P2 -->|no| M[git merge --no-edit origin/base]
  REW[test-rework mergeMain] --> P3{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P3 -->|yes| E[throw actionable refusal]
  P3 -->|no| M2[merge origin/main + auto-resolve]
```

</details>

# gh-761: WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)

## Description

**Live sequence (fa PR #1311, branch ai/gh-1308, 2026-10-06):** WIP auto-saves at 10:27/10:32/10:37 (5-min cadence), then 'Merge branch main' commit 9a7e2ae as tip. This time the merge was clean (marker scan on the branch tip: no `<<<<<<<` in dart/yaml). Same pattern on fa #1231 (saves 09:58/10:03 → merge 219f96f).

**The risk:** the autosave ticks blindly. If a merge of main CONFLICTS mid-leg, the next tick's `git add -A && git commit` will either (a) error out mid-merge (harmless but noisy), or (b) finalize the merge and bake unresolved conflict markers into a 'WIP auto-save' commit — silent branch corruption that then flows into validation/review as if it were deliberate work.

**Fix:** the autosave must skip its tick when MERGE_HEAD exists (git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD), and the merge-main step must refuse to start on a dirty tree (or autosave-then-merge atomically). Owner raised it: 'автокомиты сломаются или нет в такой ситуации?'

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

The docs-freshness check regenerates `docs/agents/generated/*` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails if the committed docs differ. The PR adds new JS files/tests but doesn't regenerate the docs. Let me check whether running the generator produces a diff on this branch.

/**
 * Shared git merge-state probes (gh-761).
 *
 * A conflicted merge of the base branch sits unconcluded in the working tree
 * (MERGE_HEAD present) until someone deliberately resolves or aborts it:
 * the rework setup leaves that state for the CLI agent on purpose, and the
 * agent's own `git merge origin/main` can be mid-conflict at any tick.
 *
 * Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before
 * touching the tree (same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js —
 * duplicated probes drift):
 *   - js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js — a blind `git add -A && git commit`
 *     would stage the unmerged paths (conflict markers included) and
 *     FINALIZE the foreign merge as a 'WIP auto-save' commit pushed to
 *     origin: silent branch corruption flowing into validation/review.
 *   - js/common/pullRequest.js syncBranchWithBase — `git merge` on top of
 *     MERGE_HEAD fails ("You have not concluded your merge") and the
 *     resolveMergeConflicts/abort fallback would then auto-resolve — or
 *     silently abort — the agent's in-flight merge.
 *   - js/storyTestAutomationRework.js mergeMain — same finalize-a-foreign-
 *     merge hazard through its --ours/--theirs auto-resolution.
 *
 * `runCommand` follows the (command, workingDir) convention shared with
 * common/pullRequest.js — pass the site's cli_execute_command wrapper so the
 * probe executes in the SAME working directory as the commit/merge it gates.
 *
 * GraalJS-compatible: var/plain functions only, no Node APIs.
 */

/**
 * True when MERGE_HEAD resolves — a merge is in progress in that working tree.
 *
 * Real git prints the merge-head SHA and exits 0 when MERGE_HEAD exists; it
 * exits 1 (cli_execute_command throws) when it doesn't. Requiring non-empty
 * output in addition to a non-throwing call keeps loose test doubles that
 * return '' for unknown commands on the "not in progress" path.
 */
function isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir) {
    if (typeof runCommand !== 'function') return false;
    try {
        var out = runCommand('git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD', workingDir);
        return !!(out && String(out).trim());
    } catch (e) {
        return false; // exit 1 — no MERGE_HEAD, the normal case
    }
}

module.exports = {
    isMergeInProgress: isMergeInProgress
};

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e

   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain

- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test

- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/762
- **Title**: gh-761 WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-761` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #761
### What changed
Mid-merge safety for the WIP autosave and the merge-main steps (gh-761): the 5-minute timer no longer commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, and every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it.

### Key decisions
- New canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` (`isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir)` via `git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites, same rationale as `gitStaging.js`
- Timer (`timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`): probe runs **before** the dirty-tree check (a mid-merge status is always dirty) and after the base-branch guard; the tick skips commit+push but still uploads the session artefact (git-independent crash-safety)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (publish-time merge): refuses as its **first** decision with `mergeInProgress: true` — previously a leftover `MERGE_HEAD` made the fallback auto-resolve or silently `git merge --abort` the agent's in-flight resolution
- `storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain`: refuses (throws actionable error) instead of `--ours`/`--theirs`-auto-committing a foreign merge with baked conflict markers

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 1659 passed, 0 failed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_timerAutoCommitAndSave.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_storyTestAutomationRework.json
node js/test/git_remote_tracking_ref.test.js
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[5-min timer tick] --> P{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P -->|yes| S[skip add/commit/push — artefact still uploaded]
  P -->|no| C[WIP auto-save commit + push]
  PUB[publish merge-main] --> P2{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P2 -->|yes| R[refuse: mergeInProgress error to ticket]
  P2 -->|no| M[git merge --no-edit origin/base]
  REW[test-rework mergeMain] --> P3{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P3 -->|yes| E[throw actionable refusal]
  P3 -->|no| M2[merge origin/main + auto-resolve]
```

</details>

# gh-761: WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)

## Description

**Live sequence (fa PR #1311, branch ai/gh-1308, 2026-10-06):** WIP auto-saves at 10:27/10:32/10:37 (5-min cadence), then 'Merge branch main' commit 9a7e2ae as tip. This time the merge was clean (marker scan on the branch tip: no `<<<<<<<` in dart/yaml). Same pattern on fa #1231 (saves 09:58/10:03 → merge 219f96f).

**The risk:** the autosave ticks blindly. If a merge of main CONFLICTS mid-leg, the next tick's `git add -A && git commit` will either (a) error out mid-merge (harmless but noisy), or (b) finalize the merge and bake unresolved conflict markers into a 'WIP auto-save' commit — silent branch corruption that then flows into validation/review as if it were deliberate work.

**Fix:** the autosave must skip its tick when MERGE_HEAD exists (git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD), and the merge-main step must refuse to start on a dirty tree (or autosave-then-merge atomically). Owner raised it: 'автокомиты сломаются или нет в такой ситуации?'

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

The docs-freshness check regenerates `docs/agents/generated/*` via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and fails if the committed docs differ. The PR adds new JS files/tests but doesn't regenerate the docs. Let me check whether running the generator produces a diff on this branch.

/**
 * Shared git merge-state probes (gh-761).
 *
 * A conflicted merge of the base branch sits unconcluded in the working tree
 * (MERGE_HEAD present) until someone deliberately resolves or aborts it:
 * the rework setup leaves that state for the CLI agent on purpose, and the
 * agent's own `git merge origin/main` can be mid-conflict at any tick.
 *
 * Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe before
 * touching the tree (same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js —
 * duplicated probes drift):
 *   - js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js — a blind `git add -A && git commit`
 *     would stage the unmerged paths (conflict markers included) and
 *     FINALIZE the foreign merge as a 'WIP auto-save' commit pushed to
 *     origin: silent branch corruption flowing into validation/review.
 *   - js/common/pullRequest.js syncBranchWithBase — `git merge` on top of
 *     MERGE_HEAD fails ("You have not concluded your merge") and the
 *     resolveMergeConflicts/abort fallback would then auto-resolve — or
 *     silently abort — the agent's in-flight merge.
 *   - js/storyTestAutomationRework.js mergeMain — same finalize-a-foreign-
 *     merge hazard through its --ours/--theirs auto-resolution.
 *
 * `runCommand` follows the (command, workingDir) convention shared with
 * common/pullRequest.js — pass the site's cli_execute_command wrapper so the
 * probe executes in the SAME working directory as the commit/merge it gates.
 *
 * GraalJS-compatible: var/plain functions only, no Node APIs.
 */

/**
 * True when MERGE_HEAD resolves — a merge is in progress in that working tree.
 *
 * Real git prints the merge-head SHA and exits 0 when MERGE_HEAD exists; it
 * exits 1 (cli_execute_command throws) when it doesn't. Requiring non-empty
 * output in addition to a non-throwing call keeps loose test doubles that
 * return '' for unknown commands on the "not in progress" path.
 */
function isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir) {
    if (typeof runCommand !== 'function') return false;
    try {
        var out = runCommand('git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD', workingDir);
        return !!(out && String(out).trim());
    } catch (e) {
        return false; // exit 1 — no MERGE_HEAD, the normal case
    }
}

module.exports = {
    isMergeInProgress: isMergeInProgress
};

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 762

- **Title**: gh-761 WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-761` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T11:42:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #761
### What changed
Mid-merge safety for the WIP autosave and the merge-main steps (gh-761): the 5-minute timer no longer commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, and every machinery merge-main step refuses to start on top of an unconcluded merge instead of finalizing it.

### Key decisions
- New canonical probe `js/common/mergeState.js` (`isMergeInProgress(runCommand, workingDir)` via `git rev-parse --quiet --verify MERGE_HEAD`) — one implementation for all commit/merge-producing sites, same rationale as `gitStaging.js`
- Timer (`timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`): probe runs **before** the dirty-tree check (a mid-merge status is always dirty) and after the base-branch guard; the tick skips commit+push but still uploads the session artefact (git-independent crash-safety)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (publish-time merge): refuses as its **first** decision with `mergeInProgress: true` — previously a leftover `MERGE_HEAD` made the fallback auto-resolve or silently `git merge --abort` the agent's in-flight resolution
- `storyTestAutomationRework.mergeMain`: refuses (throws actionable error) instead of `--ours`/`--theirs`-auto-committing a foreign merge with baked conflict markers

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 1659 passed, 0 failed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_timerAutoCommitAndSave.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_storyTestAutomationRework.json
node js/test/git_remote_tracking_ref.test.js
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[5-min timer tick] --> P{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P -->|yes| S[skip add/commit/push — artefact still uploaded]
  P -->|no| C[WIP auto-save commit + push]
  PUB[publish merge-main] --> P2{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P2 -->|yes| R[refuse: mergeInProgress error to ticket]
  P2 -->|no| M[git merge --no-edit origin/base]
  REW[test-rework mergeMain] --> P3{MERGE_HEAD?}
  P3 -->|yes| E[throw actionable refusal]
  P3 -->|no| M2[merge origin/main + auto-resolve]
```

# gh-761: WIP autosave vs merge-main race: blind 5-min auto-save can finalize a conflicted merge or bake conflict markers (live sequence: fa #1311 saves 10:27/32/37 → merge-main commit 9a7e2ae)

## Description

**Live sequence (fa PR #1311, branch ai/gh-1308, 2026-10-06):** WIP auto-saves at 10:27/10:32/10:37 (5-min cadence), then 'Merge branch main' commit 9a7e2ae as tip. This time the merge was clean (marker scan on the branch tip: no `<<<<<<<` in dart/yaml). Same pattern on fa #1231 (saves 09:58/10:03 → merge 219f96f).

**The risk:** the autosave ticks blindly. If a merge of main CONFLICTS mid-leg, the next tick's `git add -A && git commit` will either (a) error out mid-merge (harmless but noisy), or (b) finalize the merge and bake unresolved conflict markers into a 'WIP auto-save' commit — silent branch corruption that then flows into validation/review as if it were deliberate work.

**Fix:** the autosave must skip its tick when MERGE_HEAD exists (git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD), and the merge-main step must refuse to start on a dirty tree (or autosave-then-merge atomically). Owner raised it: 'автокомиты сломаются или нет в такой ситуации?'
